title: Doctors want hospitals to pool data on what Hyderabad's AQI 300 days do to us

slides.head: Doctors want hospitals to pool data on what Hyderabad's AQI 300 days do to us
What happened
slides.body: KIMS's Dr Sudheer Vinnamala proposed hospitals share anonymised data on respiratory illness, strokes and heart conditions with health authorities.

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: Hyderabad's AQI crossed 300 on Deepavali, and PM2.5 and PM10 were several times above limits, the panel heard.

slides.head: AQI on Deepavali
slides.body: About 80% of children live within 2-3 km of their school, so fixes near schools cover most trips.

slides.head: Dig deeper
slides.body: About 80% of children live within 2-3 km of their schools, PHFI research shows.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: Whether health authorities take up the hospital data-sharing idea before the winter pollution peak. Ask: What would a city health database measure first?

slides.head: Spill the tea, daily
slides.body: Hyderabad news in 30 seconds, with the numbers and the questions. Follow for tomorrow's drop: spillthetea.news

captions.instagram:
Doctors want hospitals to pool data on what Hyderabad's AQI 300 days do to us

At Cyberabad Moves, doctors from KIMS, AIG and PHFI called for hospitals to share anonymised data on pollution-linked illness.

Why it matters: Hyderabad's AQI crossed 300 on Deepavali, and PM2.5 and PM10 were several times above limits, the panel heard.

Source: The Hindu. Image: The Hindu
